newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso unveils new land reform measures.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso unveils new land reform measures.

text.p: President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, under fire for Brazil's unfair distribution of land ownership, announced new measures on Tuesday to help the landless and small plot farmers.

"This government is settling four times as many families as its predecessors," Cardoso said in a weekly radio address. "And we want to do more than settle, we want the settlements to work and the settlers to become productive farmers quickly."
Brazil has one of the world's most unequal land ownership ratios, with one percent of landowners holding about 45 percent of farmland, according to estimates by the Catholic Church.
The government is disappropriating large unused estates and allocating them to landless families. It says it is on target for its aim of settling 280,000 families in four years.

But a recent poll found 85 percent of Brazilians support the tactics of the radical Landless Movement (MST), which encourages the landless to seize and settle unused farms and accuses the government of being in the pocket of powerful land barons.
About 1,000 MST members are marching from three points in Brazil for a demonstration in the capital Brasilia on April 17, the first anniversary of a massacre of 19 landless protesters by police.

In his radio address, Cardoso said a task force comprising several ministries would speed up installation of basic infrastructure in settlements, including construction of more than 1,000 schools by the end of 1998.

The president also announced what he said was a "revolutionary" plan to decentralize land reform, giving states and municipalities powers to use their properties or buy farms and turn them over to landless families.
Another new measure would enable landless workers to take out bank loans to buy land, sidestepping the bureaucracy of the government's land reform program, Cardoso said.
